pull.title: fix(anthropic-oauth): put the subscription token where Anthropic reads it
pull.body:
## The headline

**The Claude subscription provider had never served a request.** Not "failed
sometimes" — **0 rows** out of 267,619 in the retained request log
(2026-08-01 → 2026-09-02), and no `request_attempts` row either. This PR is not
fixing failing traffic; it is turning on a provider that has been dormant since
it was written, and fixing the four independent reasons it could not have worked.

The root cause is one line. `providers/anthropic_oauth/auth.py` presented the
OAuth token in `x-api-key` and never set `Authorization` at all. Claude Code
2.1.258 puts an OAuth credential in `Authorization: Bearer` and explicitly nulls
`X-Api-Key` (binary offsets `187124317`, `181109007`, and its own in-bundle curl
example at `96384881`); `opencode-anthropic-auth@0.0.13` arrives at the same
shape independently and calls `requestHeaders.delete("x-api-key")`. The one test
covering the header set asserted the bug, and is rewritten here deliberately.

**This PR makes a dormant provider live.** That is the risk, and it is the point.

## The header table, as shipped

Inbound Claude Code request → upstream `api.anthropic.com`. Every value is either
mirrored from what the client itself sent or a documented fallback; nothing is
manufactured. `providers/anthropic_oauth/auth.py` carries this table with the
byte offsets.

| Header | MCC sends | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <access token>` | offsets 187124317 / 181109007 / 96384881; `opencode-anthropic-auth@0.0.13` |
| `x-api-key` | **never sent** | same — Claude Code nulls it whenever an OAuth credential is in play |
| `anthropic-version` | the client's value, else `2023-06-01` | offset 181109007 (`buildHeaders`) |
| `anthropic-beta` | floor `oauth-2025-04-20,claude-code-20250219` ∪ (client's list ∩ closed allow-list) | registry at offset 183023150 + 120,969 measured inbound requests |
| `user-agent` | the client's value, else `claude-cli/2.1.258 (external, cli)` | shape at offset 183634762; the old constant was `claude-cli/2.1.235.2db (external, cli)`, a `cc_version` build suffix spliced into a UA |
| `x-app` | the client's value, else `cli` | offset 187124946 — `cli-bg` is real traffic and used to be flattened to `cli` |
| `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access` | `true` | present in real inbound Claude Code traffic |
| tool names | **verbatim** | 0 hits for any `cc_` tool name in the 218 MB binary, against 137 for the real `mcp__` |

Unknown inbound betas are dropped and their names logged, never forwarded: an
unrecognised beta is the likeliest cause of a 400 that looks like a model problem.

The `cc_` prefix machinery (`tool_names.py`, `apply_tool_prefix`,
`strip_tool_prefix_from_frame`) is deleted. It was OpenCode's `mcp_` disguise
with the string swapped, and its reverse pass was a blind
`frame.replace('"name":"cc_', '"name":"')` over each SSE frame — so any *content*
containing that literal was corrupted too. A test now asserts both halves.

## The gate

**Rule (admission):** the request body's `cc_entrypoint` marker, and nothing
else. It travels in the body, so MCC can neither forge it for traffic it did not
receive nor strip it from traffic it did.

**Admitted:** `cli`, `cli-bg`, `sdk-cli`, `sdk-py`, `sdk-ts` — the Claude Code
CLI and the Claude Agent SDK, which drives the Claude Code binary. Everything
else is refused. Before this PR the gate admitted `cli` alone, which refused
**64%** of this operator's genuine Claude Code traffic (77,064 of 120,969 measured
requests are `sdk-py`) — the client Anthropic's own policy names *alongside*
Claude Code, not against it. Note also that `claude -p` reports `sdk-cli`, so
even the plain CLI in print mode was refused.

**Corroborants, recorded and never used to refuse:** the inbound
`user-agent`'s entrypoint, its version, and `x-app`, plus an `agreed` flag, are
logged on every gated request. Making them a second admission test would add a
thing to keep in sync with an upstream nobody here controls.

**Default: on.** The docs now say plainly that the marker is a *good-faith
attribution field, not an authenticator* — its value is
`process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`.

**The refusal message, verbatim from a live run:**

```
The Anthropic subscription provider only serves requests that come from Anthropic's
own clients -- the Claude Code CLI or the Claude Agent SDK. This request reports
cc_entrypoint=opencode, so it was refused rather than billed to your Claude
subscription. Route it to the `anthropic` provider (Claude Console API key)
instead, or set ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_REQUIRE_CLAUDE_CODE=false if you have read
docs/ANTHROPIC-SUBSCRIPTION.md and accept what it says. Admitted entrypoints:
cli, cli-bg, sdk-cli, sdk-py, sdk-ts.
```

## Token lifecycle, as implemented

- **Proactive and non-blocking.** Inside the 120 s leeway the credential is
  refreshed on a background task and the request in hand goes out on the token it
  already has, which is still valid. Only a genuinely expired token blocks.
- **Single-flight per credential *file*,** not per provider instance — a hot
  reload builds a second provider, and two instance-local locks let both spend the
  refresh token and clobber each other. Double-checked inside the lock: the loser
  finds a fresh credential already stored and returns it.
- **401 → refresh once, retry once,** inside the attempt the rotating loop had
  already budgeted. A second 401 is an authentication failure. Asserted at exactly
  two upstream calls, never three.
- **Refresh POST** carries `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` (offset 180990503),
  which MCC sent on no request before.
- **Endpoints** moved to Claude Code 2.1.258's (`platform.claude.com`), with the
  `console.anthropic.com` hosts kept as a documented fallback on 301/308/404.
  Login asks for the full six-scope set instead of three.
- **`refreshTokenExpiresAt` and `rateLimitTier`** survive load → store → load
  instead of being parsed away; `expiresAt` is written in milliseconds like the
  Claude Code file it mirrors, and both units still load.
- **Atomic 0600 write kept.** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is still read-only to
  MCC and never refreshed in place.
- **Raw `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN` stays non-refreshing, and is documented as
  such** — there is nothing to refresh it *with*. A comma-separated list now fails
  construction: several non-refreshing tokens are not a rotation pool, and
  rotating subscription credentials is the "unusual traffic pattern" the policy
  names.
- **No token, and no token-endpoint response body, can reach an exception
  message.** `oauth_login.py` used to put `response.text[:200]` in one.

## Live proof

> **User consent (2026-09-02 18:37): fixture replay + ≤3 tiny live requests through MCC with the user's own Claude Code subscription.**

Three live requests, no more, through a scratch MCC on `127.0.0.1:8199` with a
scratch `HOME`; the live server on `:8082` was never touched, and the operator's
real `~/.fcc/anthropic_oauth.json` and `~/.claude/.credentials.json` were read
only — never written.

| # | Request | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `claude -p "say ok"` (default model → `claude-opus-5`) | **429** `rate_limit_error`, `"Usage credits are required for long context requests."` — one of the verbatim strings decompiled from the client. **The auth layer accepted the credential**: this is an entitlement answer, not a 401. |
| 2 | `claude -p "say ok" --model sonnet` | **200**, answered `ok`. First successful `anthropic_oauth` request in the project's history. |
| 3 | same, after a server restart, to repopulate the header store | **200** |

Rate-limit headers, read from a real Anthropic response (not invented, not computed):

```
anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status            allowed
anthropic-ratelimit-unified-reset             1788393000
anthropic-ratelimit-unified-5h-utilization    0.35
anthropic-ratelimit-unified-5h-reset          1788393000
anthropic-ratelimit-unified-7d-utilization    0.41
anthropic-ratelimit-unified-7d-reset          1788433200
anthropic-ratelimit-unified-overage-status    rejected
```

Request-log rows from the scratch store:

```
provider          key_index  key_label   status       requested_model    in  out
anthropic_oauth   0          max · mcc   success      claude-sonnet-5    10   25
anthropic_oauth   0          max · mcc   rate_limit   claude-opus-5       -    -
```

Refusal proof, a hand-built non-Claude-Code request to the same scratch server
(`user-agent: opencode/1.4.0`, `cc_entrypoint=opencode`) — refused with the
message quoted above, and no upstream call made.

**The refresh path could not be proven.** The stored credential in
`~/.fcc/anthropic_oauth.json` is expired (2026-09-01 10:24, ~37 h), and every
refresh attempt against **both** hosts answered `429 rate_limit_error`
("Rate limited. Please try again later.") over ~40 minutes — not `invalid_grant`,
so the refresh token is not proven dead, only un-exercisable right now. Both
endpoints answer, so neither host is gone. The live requests therefore used the
credential Claude Code itself holds (still valid at the time, copied read-only
into the scratch store — MCC's own documented "Use Claude Code credentials"
import), which also proved `refreshTokenExpiresAt` and `rateLimitTier` end to end
on real data. **Action required for the operator: sign in again with
`mcc-anthropic-oauth-login` if the refresh continues to fail.**

## Dashboard

Screenshots in `screenshots-oauth-pr/` (tokens masked, zero console errors):
`card-live-credential-900.png`, `card-live-credential-1600.png`,
`card-expired-credential-900.png`, `card-no-credential-900.png`.

Live card content, verbatim:

```
Plan                  max
Rate-limit tier       default_claude_max_5x
Credential source     mcc
Access token expires  9/3/2026, 1:59:51 AM (in 2 h)
Refresh token expires 9/5/2026, 10:48:54 PM (in 71 h)
Scopes                user:file_upload user:inference user:mcp_servers user:profile user:sessions:claude_code
5-hour window used    0.35
5-hour window resets  9/3/2026, 2:50:00 AM (1788393000)
Weekly window used    0.41
Weekly window resets  9/3/2026, 2:00:00 PM (1788433200)
Overage               rejected
Anthropic says        allowed
```

Before any response has carried a header the windows read the literal
**`not yet observed`**, and "you hit your 5-hour window, it resets at …" appears
only when the header says `session-limit-reached`. An expired token and a
credential missing `user:inference` are flagged in red. `window.prompt` for the
login code is replaced by an inline field that restates the warning above it.

## Tests

New `tests/providers/test_anthropic_oauth_wire.py` (28) —
`test_oauth_token_is_presented_as_a_bearer_not_an_api_key`,
`test_beta_header_is_the_floor_unioned_with_the_clients_own`,
`test_unknown_client_betas_are_dropped_and_reported`,
`test_user_agent_and_x_app_mirror_the_client`,
`test_installed_fingerprint_reaches_the_upstream_headers`,
`test_tool_names_are_sent_and_returned_verbatim`,
`test_refresh_leeway_is_two_minutes`,
`test_concurrent_refreshes_perform_one_exchange_across_two_providers`,
`test_refresh_sends_the_oauth_beta_header`,
`test_a_refresh_error_never_carries_a_response_body`,
`test_a_401_refreshes_once_and_retries_once`,
`test_a_second_401_is_an_authentication_failure`,
`test_refresh_token_expiry_and_rate_limit_tier_round_trip`,
`test_stored_expiry_is_milliseconds_and_both_units_load`,
`test_login_requests_the_full_claude_code_scope_set`,
`test_authorize_url_uses_the_current_host`,
`test_unified_rate_limit_headers_are_captured`,
`test_a_real_response_populates_the_observer`,
`test_key_label_names_the_plan_and_the_source`,
`test_a_comma_separated_raw_token_is_refused`,
`test_cache_control_survives_to_the_wire` (closes the `WORKING-NOTES` §45
question for the native path: **CONFIRMED**, `cache_control` reaches the wire),
`test_recorded_claude_code_session_replays_end_to_end`.

New `tests/api/test_admin_anthropic_oauth_card.py` (3) and four jsdom tests
covering the card's live, unobserved and absent states.

`tests/providers/test_anthropic_oauth.py` rewritten where it locked in the bug:
`test_oauth_headers_are_the_claude_code_set` asserted
`headers["x-api-key"] == _TOKEN` and now asserts the Bearer with no `x-api-key`
at all; `test_agent_sdk_is_not_treated_as_the_cli` becomes
`test_the_agent_sdk_is_an_anthropic_client_but_not_the_terminal`; the three
`cc_` prefix tests are deleted; the leeway test is retuned to 120 s. Every other
test in that file is unchanged and passing.

The fixture is a **real** Claude Code 2.1.258 request recorded through
`scripts/dev/record_anthropic_oauth_exchange.py` (no upstream call, no
credential), redacted — the script refuses to write a file containing `sk-ant`
— and trimmed to four tool definitions and one turn, with the operator's
environment digest dropped. Its headers, billing marker and identity block are
exactly as they arrived.

**Counts.** `52 passed` for the two provider files; `203 passed` for
`tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` alone with `-n 0` (199 before, +4);
`8716 passed, 38 skipped, 14 failed` for the full suite with a redirected HOME.
All 14 are the known local baseline (PowerShell installer tests and
`EXA_API_KEY`/`ddgs` env leakage) and none is in a file this PR touches — the
recorded baseline is 15. `ruff format --check` repo-wide, `ruff check` and `ty`
are all clean, with no suppressions added.

## Deviations from the spec

- **No new `params` keys in the request log.** R17's corroboration is a
  structured log line rather than a `params` field, to keep the request-log
  schema out of a wire-shape PR.
- **`x-claude-code-session-id` / `-agent-id` / `-parent-agent-id` are not
  mirrored** and `ALLOWED_HEADERS` is unchanged. They are correlation ids for a
  session MCC is not, and mirroring them would put a client-side identifier into
  durable storage for no diagnostic gain.
- **`key_label` is `"<plan> · <source>"`** (`max · mcc`), per Q7 — MCC never
  fetches the profile, so there is no email to use and adding a `user:profile`
  call per credential for a log label would be a new upstream request.
- **No `JOURNAL.md` entry**: the file the spec's §7 names does not exist on this
  base.
- Version is **6.36.0** (MINOR) from 6.35.1, not the spec's 6.33.0 → 6.34.0.

## Residual risks

- **A dormant provider is now live.** With the gate on and widened, the Agent SDK
  traffic that used to be refused will now reach the subscription credential. That
  is the requested behaviour and it is a real increase in volume against the
  account.
- **Merging the client's betas can surface an entitlement 429/400.** Live request
  #1 hit exactly that: the client sent `context-1m-2025-08-07` and the account
  answered "Usage credits are required for long context requests." The alternative
  — dropping the beta — would silently cap a 1M-context session at 200k, so the
  merge stands and the upstream body is surfaced in the error.
- **SUSPECTED, still:** that `x-api-key` is *what* 401s. Nothing proves it,
  because nothing ever ran; what is now CONFIRMED is that the Bearer shape is
  accepted. **UNVERIFIED:** whether the `console.anthropic.com` fallback path is
  ever exercised — both hosts answered 429 throughout.
- **The refresh path is untested against a live 200.** It is covered by fixture
  tests only; every real attempt was rate-limited.
- **The gate is not an authenticator.** Anything that sets
  `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` and reuses Claude Code's system-prompt shape can claim
  an admitted entrypoint. The docs say so now.
- **It cannot protect an already-flagged account,** and this PR does not change
  Anthropic's position that none of this is permitted.

commit.message:
fix(anthropic-oauth): put the subscription token where Anthropic reads it

The Claude subscription provider had never served a request. Not "failed
sometimes" -- zero rows in 267,619 logged requests over a month, and no
`request_attempts` row either. The reason is one line: `auth.py` presented the
OAuth token in `x-api-key` and never set `Authorization` at all. Claude Code
2.1.258 puts an OAuth credential in `Authorization: Bearer` and explicitly
nulls `X-Api-Key` (binary offsets 187124317 and 181109007); the independent
`opencode-anthropic-auth` plugin deletes `x-api-key` for the same reason. The
one test that covered the header set asserted the bug.

So the wire shape is now Claude Code's, with the values mirrored from the
inbound request rather than invented:

  Authorization  Bearer <access token>; x-api-key never sent
  anthropic-beta MCC's floor unioned with the client's own list, intersected
                 with a closed allow-list decompiled from the client's beta
                 registry plus what 120,969 measured requests actually carried
  user-agent     the client's, else claude-cli/2.1.258 (external, cli) -- the
                 old constant spliced a cc_version build suffix into a UA
  x-app          the client's, so cli-bg stops being flattened to cli
  anthropic-version  the client's, else 2023-06-01

The `cc_` tool-name prefix is gone. A full scan of the 218 MB Claude Code
binary finds zero occurrences of any `cc_` tool name against 137 for the real
`mcp__` prefix: the machinery was OpenCode's `mcp_` disguise with the string
swapped, and its reverse pass was a blind string replace over each SSE frame,
so any content containing the literal was corrupted too. Tool names now go out
verbatim.

The gate is widened and stays on by default. It used to admit `cc_entrypoint=cli`
alone, which refused the Claude Agent SDK -- 64% of this operator's genuine
Claude Code traffic, and the client Anthropic's own policy names alongside
Claude Code. The admitted set is now cli, cli-bg, sdk-cli, sdk-py, sdk-ts;
every other harness is still refused, now with a message naming
ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_REQUIRE_CLAUDE_CODE. The body marker remains the only
admission rule -- MCC can neither forge nor strip it -- and the inbound
user-agent and x-app are recorded beside it as corroborants, never as a second
test. The docs now say plainly that the marker is a good-faith attribution
field, not an authenticator.

Around that, the credential's own lifecycle: refresh is proactive and
non-blocking, so a token inside its 120 s leeway is renewed in the background
while the request in hand goes out on the credential it already has; only an
expired token blocks. Single-flight moved from per provider instance to per
credential file with a double check inside the lock, because a hot reload
builds a second provider and two instance-local locks let both spend the
refresh token. A 401 refreshes once and retries once, inside the attempt the
rotating loop already budgeted. The refresh POST carries the
`anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` the client sends, the token endpoint moved
to the 2.1.258 hosts with the old ones as a documented 404/301 fallback, and
login asks for Claude Code's full six-scope set instead of three.
`refreshTokenExpiresAt` and `rateLimitTier` are no longer parsed away, and
`expiresAt` is written in milliseconds like the file it mirrors. Neither a
token nor a token endpoint's response body can reach an exception message.

The dashboard card reports what MCC holds and what Anthropic said: plan,
rate-limit tier, both expiries, the scopes with `user:inference` flagged when
absent, and the 5-hour and weekly windows read from
`anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` response headers. No window is ever computed --
before a real response carries one the card says "not yet observed", and
"you hit your 5-hour window" is only ever repeated from a header. The pasted
login code moved from `window.prompt` to an inline field that restates the
warning above it. A request-log row for this provider now carries a `key_label`
that means something (`max · mcc`) instead of the same masked reference string
every OAuth row shared.

Verified against the real thing: a recorded Claude Code 2.1.258 session replays
through a stubbed transport and asserts the exact upstream header set, and
three live requests through a scratch MCC on a scratch port confirmed the
Bearer shape is accepted, captured genuine `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*`
values, and produced the first successful `anthropic_oauth` row that has ever
existed.
